sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V. Act')by the claimant challenging the judgment of dismissal passed in MVC No.289/2011 dated 18.04.2012 by the Additional District Judge & MACT, Fast Track Court-I, Hassan.
2.
For the sake of convenience, parties herein are referred with the original ranks occupied by them before the Trial Court.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that, on 04.09.2010 at 9.30 pm when the petitioner was coming back from his agriculture land with his brother-in- law on the left side of the road, the rider of the motor bike NC: 2023:KHC:40552 bearing Reg.No.KA.41-Q-7202, drove the same in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.

As a result petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he was immediately shifted to S.S.M Hospital,
Hassan and thereafter, he was shifted to Vikram Hospital, Mysore wherein, he was treated as an in-patient.
As he suffered grievous injuries, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
The claim petition was objected by the respondents.

4. After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the claimant has failed to establish that, the injuries were because of the accident as asserted by the claimant.
5. Being aggrieved by this judgment the claimant is before this Court by way of this appeal.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurance Company.
Perused the records.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant would contend that the records in the form of Ex.P3 and Ex.P4 as well as Ex.C3 clearly disclose that the claimant has suffered grievous injuries due to hitting of offending vehicle and the Tribunal has erroneously observed that, the claimant has failed to establish that the accident is because of involvement of offending vehicle and hence, he would seek for setting aside the impugned judgment of dismissal.
Alternatively, he would also seek for remand of the matter in order to give an opportunity to the claimant to examine the relevant witnesses and produce material documents to substantiate his claim.

8. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 would contend that, though the accident has occurred on 04.09.2010 at 9.30 pm, the complaint was lodged on 24.10.2010 at 6.00 pm, after the delay of 44 NC: 2023:KHC:40552 days, and he would also contend that the original discharge summary was not produced and only a copy was produced wherein there is an endorsement asserting that the original was handed over to the brother of the claimant.

He would also assert that the initial history given before Vikram Hospital was fall from two wheeler and subsequently, a new story was invented regarding hitting by the two wheeler and hence, he would contend that the Tribunal has appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper prospective and has rightly dismissed the claim petition.
Hence, sought for dismissal of appeal.
9. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, there is no serious dispute of the fact that the claimant has suffered accidental injuries on 04.09.2010 at 9.30 pm.
The claimant is placing reliance on Ex.C3 wherein there is a history given as RTA asserting that, while the patient was walking on the road he was hit by a two wheeler from rear end.

However, on perusal of Ex.C3 NC:
2023:KHC:40552 in detail, it is evident that Ex.C3 is a duplicate copy and there is an endorsement on the top asserting that the original discharge summary was handed over to the patient's brother on 05.12.2011.

There is no explanation from the claimant as to why he has not produced the original discharge summary and why he has again produced a duplicate copy of discharge summary obtained from the Vikram Hospital.

On perusal of the Ex.C3 out- patient assessment sheet there is a clear endorsement in hand writing in the history sheet dated 05.09.2010 at 2.10 am wherein there is a specific reference that the alleged history of RTA and patient was riding a two wheeler when he sustained a self fall on 04.09.2010 at around 9.30 pm at a village near Hassan.
This history was given before the Vikram Hospital when the patient was admitted in the Vikram Hospital at 2.10 am.
10. Admittedly, the patient was referred to Vikram Hospital by S.S.M Hospital wherein the claimant was given a First Aid.
Interestingly, the medical records pertaining to NC: 2023:KHC:40552 S.S.M Hospital were not produced so as to prove what was the history given before the S.S.M Hospital.
11. Further the allegations of the claimant disclose that he was walking on road on 04.09.2010 at 9.30 pm along with his brother-in-law when a two wheeler hit him.
In that event, nothing prevented his brother-in-law from lodging a complaint immediately.
The records disclose that the brother of the claimant has also received the original records and further he has got rectified the history given before the Vikram Hospital by submitting an affidavit.
In that event, what prevented him from lodging the complaint is not at all forthcoming.

Though the accident has occurred on 04.09.2010,
the intimation from Vikram Hospital was issued on 21.10.2010 after 44 days and the complaint was lodged later on 24th i.e after nearly 46 days.

This delay is not explained and from the records itself,

3 it is evident that the claimant has suffered injuries by self fall from a two wheeler, but subsequently,
they wanted to fix a two wheeler in order to have unlawful NC: 2023:KHC:40552 claim.

sentences.text: There is an inordinate delay in lodging the complaint which is not properly explained and further the original discharge summary or original documents pertaining to S.S.M Hospital, Hassan were not produced.
The Tribunal has appreciated all these aspects and has rightly observed that claimant has failed to establish that he was hit by a two wheeler so as to claim compensation.
No illegality or perversity is found in the judgment of dismissal passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, the claim petition being devoid of any merits does not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, the appeal stands dismissed.
